paper.title: What Do We Care About in Bandits with Noncompliance? BRACE: Bandits with Recommendations, Abstention, and Certified Effects

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-context square-IV bandit with noncompliance, REC objective (identification of operational optimum)
unmapped: Noncompliance: learner chooses a recommendation (instrument) Z in [K]; realized treatment X=C(Z) is determined by a latent compliance type and is observed along with the reward
Target is the best policy in a finite policy class Pi mapping finite contexts to recommendations (operational recommendation welfare)
Finite context set of size S with i.i.d. contexts and marginal nu(w)>0
settings.definition_quote: Assume the context space is finite, $\W=\{1,\dots,S\}$. At each round, an i.i.d. draw $(W_t,C_t,Y_t(1),\dots,Y_t(K))$ is generated from a stationary population, with context marginal $\nu(w)>0$ for every $w\in\W$. The learner observes $W_t$, then selects $Z_t\in[K]$ ... and then observes $X_t=C_t(Z_t), Y_t=Y_t(X_t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-context square-IV bandit with noncompliance, REC objective (operational regret)
unmapped: Noncompliance: learner chooses a recommendation Z; realized treatment X=C(Z) observed with reward
Regret measured against the best policy in a finite policy class Pi over finite contexts (operational recommendation welfare)
settings.definition_quote: Operational Recommendation Welfare (REC): $V^{\mathrm{rec}}(\pi_{\mathrm{rec}}) := \E[Y(C(\pi_{\mathrm{rec}}(W)))]$. This is the value of deploying the recommendation policy in the current workflow, including downstream overrides.

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-context square-IV bandit with noncompliance, TRT objective (structural treatment-policy identification)
unmapped: Noncompliance / instrument-armed: learner plays recommendations Z but the target is the best structural treatment policy (counterfactual direct control), identified via IV inversion mu(w)=P(w)^{-1} g(w)
Finite policy class Pi over finite contexts
Contextual homogeneity (Assumption 4.1) and invertible compliance matrices (Assumption 4.2)
settings.definition_quote: Structural Treatment Welfare (TRT): $V^{\mathrm{str}}(\pi_{\mathrm{str}}) := \E[Y(\pi_{\mathrm{str}}(W))]$. This asks what would happen in a counterfactual regime with direct treatment control.

symbols.Delta_rec: gap between the best and second-best recommendation policy values in Pi

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Operational identification and regret (REC). Suppose the REC objective is selected and $\Delta_{\mathrm{rec}}>0$. Then BRACE commits only to the true operational optimum $\pi^\star_{\mathrm{rec}}$. Moreover, up to logarithmic factors in $S,K,|\Pi|,1/\delta$, $\tau_{\mathrm{rec}} = \tilde{\mathcal O}(K/(\nu_{\min}\Delta_{\mathrm{rec}}^2))$ samples suffice for commitment.

results.notes: Holds with probability at least 1-delta; hidden log factors in S,K,|Pi|,1/delta. Only a proof sketch is given.

symbols.Delta_rec: gap between the best and second-best recommendation policy values in Pi

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Since REC incurs zero additional operational regret after correct commitment, its total operational regret up to any horizon $T$ is $\mathcal O(\tau_{\mathrm{rec}})$ on the good event.

results.notes: Paper states O(tau_rec) on the good event (prob >= 1-delta); combined with tau_rec = Õ(K/(nu_min Delta_rec^2)). Regret here is operational (recommendation-welfare) regret; whether in means or realized is not specified.

symbols.Delta_str: gap between the best and second-best structural treatment policy values in Pi

conditions: Assumption 4.2: compliance matrix P(w) invertible for every context
Assumption 4.1 (contextual homogeneity), used via Lemma 4.3 for IV identification

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Structural identification (TRT). Suppose the TRT objective is selected, $\Delta_{\mathrm{str}}>0$, and Assumption~\ref{asm:id} holds. Then BRACE stops only after identifying the true structural optimum $\pi^\star_{\mathrm{str}}$. Up to logarithmic factors in $S,K,|\Pi|,1/\delta$, $\tau_{\mathrm{str}} = \tilde{\mathcal O}(L^2K/(\nu_{\min}\Delta_{\mathrm{str}}^2))$ samples suffice for identification.

results.notes: Theorem explicitly requires only Assumption 4.2, but validity of the structural intervals relies on Lemma 4.3 which needs homogeneity; recorded as condition. Probability >= 1-delta; proof sketch only.
